text: The SDK requires Python 3.10 or newer.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md: The minimum supported version is now 3.11.
note: 2.0.0 dropped Python 3.10 and pyproject.toml says requires-python >=3.11; the memory also says 3.11 is the oldest supported version.

text: Python 3.11 is the oldest version the SDK supports.
note: requires-python >=3.11 makes 3.11 the minimum; the memory's other line claims 3.10 still works.

text: make test runs ruff and mypy before the test suite.
note: make test only runs pytest (the Makefile agrees); lint and type checks are part of make check, the line next to it.

text: Run make check before opening a pull request.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md: Run `make check` locally before you open a pull request.
note: CONTRIBUTING asks for make check before a pull request; the memory states this twice.

text: The nightly live job seems to run at 03:00 UTC.
note: The schedule is cron 0 3 * * * in UTC (comment above it) and the live job only runs for scheduled builds; the claim is hedged with 'seems'.

text: Live tests need the QUAYSIDE_API_KEY environment variable.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md: Live tests authenticate with `QUAYSIDE_SANDBOX_KEY`, not with `QUAYSIDE_API_KEY`.
note: Live tests use QUAYSIDE_SANDBOX_KEY; QUAYSIDE_API_KEY is the production key the client reads by default.

text: Failures of the nightly live job are probably sandbox outages, not SDK bugs.
note: The evidence describes when and how the live job runs, never why it fails.

text: mypy is pinned to 1.11.2 because 1.12 breaks the pydantic plugin.
note: The dev group pins mypy==1.11.2 and enables the pydantic.mypy plugin, but no file gives a reason for the pin, so the claimed cause is unsupported.

text: The client retries a failed request 3 times before giving up.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md: now counts the first request, so a failing call is retried at most twice
note: Since 2.0.0 MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 includes the first request, so there are at most two retries; three retries was the 1.x behaviour.

text: The client retries on any 5xx response.
evidence: src/quayside/client.py: # 500 is not retried: the API returns it for request bugs that a retry cannot fix.
note: RETRY_STATUSES is 429, 502, 503 and 504; 500 is explicitly not retried.

text: The retry loop parses Retry-After as a number of seconds.
evidence: src/quayside/client.py: # The Quayside API sends Retry-After in seconds, never as an HTTP date.
note: The seconds-only comment and float conversion directly entail the parsing behavior; this describes code, not a speculative inference.

text: Catching QuaysideError handles every failure the SDK can raise.
evidence: src/quayside/errors.py: Network errors from httpx (timeouts, connection failures) propagate unchanged.
note: Only API-reported errors are QuaysideError subclasses; httpx timeouts and connection errors escape it.

text: The production API currently allows 60 requests per minute per key.
note: The SDK handles 429 and Retry-After but no file states the API's rate limit.

text: Release 1.8.0, shipped on 2026-02-03, added retries for HTTP 429.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md: Retry on HTTP 429, honouring the `Retry-After` header.
note: The 1.8.0 (2026-02-03) changelog entry adds 429 retries; the date is over 180 days before as_of.

text: Never import requests in the SDK package.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md: Do not import `requests` anywhere under `src/quayside/`.
note: CONTRIBUTING forbids importing requests under src/quayside; the rule is stated with absolute wording.
CONTRIBUTING says to rebase on main before review and to get one approval; it never says how pull requests are merged.

text: The publish stage waits for a manual approval before uploading to PyPI.
note: The publish stage runs after the check stage on v* tags; neither the pipeline nor CONTRIBUTING mentions an approval gate.
